answer: A gemstone grading report anchors each seat. The miner buys one rough stone, has a lab weigh it to a milligram, chart its inclusions and laser-inscribe the seat hash on the girdle. When the seed names an hour, the seat photographs that inscription under a loupe beside the epoch number. Two seats filing one dealer lot, or stones sharing an inclusion map, fold into one vote and forfeit 60,000 POA. Rough jade costs $12, grading $60, inscription $8, insured post $18: 1,000 seats run $98,000. A mesa looks like one rock until you walk its rim; each pocket of onyx shows veins no twin shares.
